eligibility.quote: I misconfigured the version macro with #3080. It is a GTE and not a GT macro
eligibility.reason: Agree with E1, E2 step 6, E4, and the overall existence of an eligible library-interface failure; disagree with the specification's E3 justification and UPGRADE operation. The failing consumer selects the newer const-reference declaration while paired with the older provider. S1 defines UPGRADE in the opposite direction. This is eligible as PAIR: the installed provider declaration is consumed by the test package's override at build time, not as a forward provider upgrade.

supporting_evidence.quote: The breaking PR was released with 31.0.0

failed_conditions.quote: error: ‘void MockExecutor::add_node(const rclcpp::node_interfaces::NodeBaseInterface::SharedPtr&, bool)’ marked ‘override’, but does not override
failed_conditions.reason: add_node remains present, but its provider declaration differs between the by-value and const-reference revisions. The consumer selects the wrong signature. element_retyped captures this declaration mismatch, even though the observed skew is not a forward UPGRADE.

loudness.reason: The compiler explicitly rejects the incompatible override.

detection_stage.reason: The failure is compilation, hence build, not a running ABI failure.

resolution.reason: The fix changes the guard to the actual release boundary. The examined primary evidence supports the correction but does not identify both installed/tested revisions of a successful resolved pair, so recommended is warranted.

notes: The eligibility disagreement is specifically the invalid UPGRADE assignment, not an internal/build-only exclusion. A declaration/override incompatibility is an interface failure even when it prevents compilation. Do not turn the earlier, distinct forward-upgrade incident into this case.
